item.title: Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo found guilty of murdering Dr Leli Darling
item.description: Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo has been found guilty of murdering Nadi based Doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya, who was also known as Leighley Leli Darling. Rokoralovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife at the deceased's residence in Fatima Court, Martintar, Nadi between 31st August and 1st September last year .
item.content:encoded:
Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo has been found guilty of murdering Nadi based Doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya, who was also known as Leighley Leli Darling.

Rokoralovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife at the deceased's residence in Fatima Court, Martintar, Nadi between 31st August and 1st September last year .

During the trial, it was heard that Rokoralovo and Dr Biumaitotoya were involved in acomplex personal relationship marked by financial dependence, jealousy, alcohol abuse and escalating conflict, culminating in a fatal attack at the deceased's home.

The prosecution said following an argument, Rokoralovo repeatedly attacked the Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife, causing fatal injuries, before leaving the scene in the deceased's vehicle.

The matter has been adjourned to the 4th of September.

item.title: 17-year-old questioned over alleged temple theft in Howell Road
item.description: A 17 year old boy is being questioned in relation to an alleged case of sacrilege whereby money was stolen from a temple in Howell Road yesterday morning. Police say the matter was reported yesterday morning.
item.content:encoded:
A 17 year old boy is being questioned in relation to an alleged case of sacrilege whereby money was stolen from a temple in Howell Road yesterday morning.

Police say the matter was reported yesterday morning.

A temple committee member told fijivillage News that $2,000 was stolen among other items.

We have also received information that the juvenile was also involved in another temple break in in Nasinu two weeks ago, we are following up with Police regarding this.

The juvenile is currently in custody at the Samabula Police Station as investigations continue.

item.title: Government reviews 26 iTaukei laws as Opposition raises concerns about uncertainty
item.description: Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga says its review of laws affecting iTaukei land, resources and traditional institutions is aimed at strengthening rights and correcting past concerns, while Opposition MP Jone Usamate says any changes must be based on truth and goodwill and should clearly benefit iTaukei people. While delivering his ministerial statement, Turaga says 26 laws introduced between
item.content:encoded:
Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga says its review of laws affecting iTaukei land, resources and traditional institutions is aimed at strengthening rights and correcting past concerns, while Opposition MP Jone Usamate says any changes must be based on truth and goodwill and should clearly benefit iTaukei people.

While delivering his ministerial statement, Turaga says 26 laws introduced between 2007 and 2022 had been identified for review, with nine already repealed, amended or superseded.

Turaga says the Government's approach is anchored in the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and that reforms must be undertaken through consultation and within Fiji's constitutional and legal framework.

While responding in the iTaukei language, Usamate says Opposition MPs are ready to assist with the review but questioned the need for changes that could create fear or uncertainty among iTaukei communities.

He says no iTaukei land was sold between 2007 and 2022 and highlighted developments during the period, including improved access to electricity and water, bridge construction and changes to the administration of iTaukei land and lease money.

Usamate is urging the Government to ensure any changes to existing laws preserve measures that have benefited iTaukei people.

He also welcomed the re-establishment of the Great Council of Chiefs but called on the Government not to politicise chiefs and traditional leaders.

Turaga then says Government will not trade one injustice for another and that reforms must address legitimate grievances without creating new legal uncertainty for landowners, families and communities.

He says the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Bill 2025 is before the Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights, while work is also progressing on the Traditional Knowledge and Cultural Expressions Bill.

Turaga adds that the Constitutional Reform Commission had completed its nationwide consultations and is finalising its report for submission to the President on the 31st of this month.

item.title: Fiji and US strengthen maritime security through joint operations
item.description: The safety and security of sailors and vessels operating in Fiji’s waters will be supported through joint maritime law enforcement operations between Fiji and the United States this week. The crew of the US Coast Guard Cutter Joseph Gerczak is visiting Suva to work alongside Fiji in bilateral maritime law enforcement operations within Fiji’s Exclusive Economic Zone.
item.content:encoded:
The safety and security of sailors and vessels operating in Fiji’s waters will be supported through joint maritime law enforcement operations between Fiji and the United States this week.

The crew of the US Coast Guard Cutter Joseph Gerczak is visiting Suva to work alongside Fiji in bilateral maritime law enforcement operations within Fiji’s Exclusive Economic Zone.

The US Coast Guard says the joint effort enables Fiji to conduct maritime shiprider operations to ensure the safety and security of sailors and vessels of all nations.

It says the partnership will help Fiji confront direct threats to its sovereignty and economy, including illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, drug trafficking and other transnational crimes .

The US Coast Guard says together with Fiji, it can help deter these illegal activities and promote regional security and a free, open and prosperous Pacific.

The Joseph Gerczak is in Fiji on behalf of Operation Blue Pacific, a multi-mission US Coast Guard initiative promoting regional stability and security throughout the Pacific.

The cutter recently assisted the Republic of the Marshall Islands with maritime law enforcement operations.

The US Coast Guard says the Joseph Gerczak’s presence in Fiji is rooted in longstanding friendships and shared values with partners and communities in the region.

The vessel is a 154-foot Fast Response Cutter with a 24-person crew.

It was the 26th Sentinel-class cutter built in the series and is the second of its class to be homeported in Honolulu.

The US Coast Guard says Operation Blue Pacific involves cutters, aircrews and personnel deploying throughout Oceania to maintain unrestricted and lawful access to the maritime domain for all nations, improve regional stability and strengthen the Coast Guard as a reliable partner for maritime safety, security and stewardship in the Pacific.

item.title: Yat Sen Primary students prepare to mark 90th Anniversary
item.description: Yat Sen Primary School students are stepping up preparations for the school’s 90th anniversary celebrations by showcasing their talents through performances. The school will celebrate the 90th anniversary of its primary school and the 40th anniversary of its secondary school from the 17th to the 20th of September.
item.content:encoded:
Yat Sen Primary School students are stepping up preparations for the school’s 90th anniversary celebrations by showcasing their talents through performances.

The school will celebrate the 90th anniversary of its primary school and the 40th anniversary of its secondary school from the 17th to the 20th of September.

Yat Sen Primary School Assistant Head Teacher Meli Yabakivou says students have formed groups and are putting a lot of effort into preparing their performances.

Yabakivou says some students have hired choreographers to help with their routines, while others are creating their own performances.

He says students are using their spare time to prepare and are looking forward to performing during the celebrations.

Assistant Head Teacher highlights the anniversaries are important milestones in the school’s history.

He says students are also balancing preparations for the celebrations with short tests, rugby and other school activities.

Yabakivou stresses despite their busy schedule, the students remain focused on what they need to do.

He says he is proud of the students for showcasing what Yat Sen has to offer and has also acknowledged the support of parents and former students.

Yat Sen alumna Soeri Rokoiga has also praised the students for the time and effort they are putting into their performances .

Rokoiga says the performances showcase the students’ talents and highlight the multicultural nature of Yat Sen.

Students, staff, parents, alumni and former scholars are expected to be part of the milestone celebrations in September.
